p:cNvPr.descr: The nucleic acids are color coded and take on various shapes. A is shaded blue and consists of a pentagonal shape bonded to a hexagonal shape. G has the same structure but is shaded green. T is a yellow shaded hexagon; C is a pink shaded hexagon. The 5’ up half of the strand has the sugar backbone consisting of small pentoses linked by phosphodiester bonds, where only the O is visible. The order of the nucleic acids from top to bottom is: CAATCGTCA. The other side, the 3’ up half, also has the sugar backbone with the small pentoses linked by phosphodiester bonds. Its order, from the top down, is GTTAGCAGT. Toward the top, an AT pair is boxed; toward the bottom, a GC pair is boxed. Both have arrows extending toward the right. The arrow from the AT box points to an enlarged image of its structure. On the left, the adenine has a 6-sided ring with 2 N and 3 double bonds, and a 5-sided ring with 2N and 2 double bonds. The bottom N of the 6-sided ring bonds left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to C, which bonds up to N, which bonds left and right to H. C double bonds down and right to N. N bonds down to C, which single bonds down and right to H and which double bonds down and left to the initial N. The double carbon bond on the left side is shared by the 5-sided ring. For the 5-sided ring, the top right C double bonds down to C, which bonds left to N, which bonds down and left to C-1’ and up to C. C bonds up and left to H and double bonds up and right to N. N bonds down and right to the starting C. This is the adenine ring. To the right, the thymine consists of a single 6-sided ring. The top C bonds up to CH3 and double bonds down and right to C, which bonds right to H and down to N. N bonds down and right to C-1’ and left to C. C double bonds down to O and up and left to N, which bonds left to H and up to C, which double bonds up and left to O and up & right to the initial C. The double bonded O on the left side of the thymine ring forms a hydrogen bond with the substituent H on the adenine ring. These are shown as vertical parallel blue lines. The bond measure is bracketed above and shown as 2.8 Angstroms (pink). The left H from the thymine ring and the right N in the adenine ring have also hydrogen bonded, with a bond length of 3.0 Angstroms. From C-1’ to C-1’ at the bottom of the pair, the measure is shown to be 11.1 Angstroms, shown with brackets (in pink). Below is the close-up visual of the CG pair. On the left, the guanine has a 6-sided ring with 2 N and 3 double bonds, and a 5-sided ring with 2N and 2 double bonds. The bottom N of the 6-sided ring bonds left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to O. C double bonds down and right to N. N bonds down to C, which single bonds down and right to N, which bonds left and right to H. C double bonds down and left to the initial N. The double carbon bond on the left side is shared by the 5-sided ring. For the 5-sided ring, the top right C double bonds down to C, which bonds left to N, which bonds down and left to C-1’ and up to C. C bonds up and left to H and double bonds up and right to N. N bonds down and right to the starting C. This is the guanine molecule. To the right, the cytosine consists of a single 6-sided ring. The top C bonds up to H and double bonds down and right to C, which bonds right to H and down to N. N bonds down and right to C-1’ and left to C. C double bonds down to O and up and left to N, which double bonds up to C, which double bonds up and left to N, which bonds left and right to H, and C bonds and up & right to the initial C. Here there are 3 hydrogen bonds: 1 between the O and H near the tops of the molecules (measure of 2.9 Angstroms, bracketed and shown in pink); 1 between H and N near the middle of the molecules (measure of 3.0 Angstroms); 1 between H and O near the bottoms of the molecules (measure of 2.9 Angstroms). The length from C-1’ to C-1’ across the whole pair is 10.8 Angstroms, bracketed at the bottom and shown in pink.
